input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale:
Section 9 contains only cause-based exits (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/SLA/legal failures) plus force majeure in 27.3; there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere (no 9.4 exists), and Section 2.1 affirmatively strips termination rights across a three-year take-or-pay commitment (Section 8.1 term is three years). That is walk-away territory under the rule: no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term. Vendor has no convenience right, which is consistent with the preferred position and is preserved. We inserted a new Section 9.4 at the preferred position (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right) and conformed Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language does not nullify it; the fallback (60 days plus a fee capped at three months' Fees) is offered in the comment.</rationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.86

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; carve it out of the take-or-pay commitment.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a convenience exit: this is a three-year commitment and Section 9 gives us only cause-based and force-majeure exits, so we have added a Customer right to terminate on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees and conformed Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay commitment does not override it. If helpful, we can discuss 60 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall have no further payment obligation for the terminated Services. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction rights, except that the commitment is subject to Customer's termination rights under Section 9, including termination for convenience under Section 9.4, and ceases to accrue for periods after the effective date of any such termination.
